summary: Rivastigmine is a reversible inhibitor of both acetyl- and butyryl-cholinesterase used for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's dementia and dementia of Parkinson's disease. It is titrated slowly (oral 1.5 mg BID up; transdermal patch 4.6 to 9.5 to 13.3 mg/24h) to limit cholinergic GI effects. Stopping for more than several days requires re-titration from the lowest dose to avoid severe vomiting.
indications: Mild to moderate dementia of the Alzheimer's type
Mild to moderate dementia associated with Parkinson's disease

dosage.d: Start 1.5 mg twice daily; increase by 1.5 mg BID at >=2-week intervals to 3-6 mg twice daily
Start 4.6 mg/24h; after >=4 weeks increase to 9.5 mg/24h; max 13.3 mg/24h
dosage.n: Rotate site; remove old patch before applying new

admin: Take oral capsules/solution twice daily WITH FOOD (morning and evening) to reduce nausea/vomiting
Apply one transdermal patch once daily to clean, dry, hairless intact skin (upper/lower back, arm or chest); rotate sites and do not apply to the same site within 14 days
Remove the previous patch before applying a new one - applying multiple patches has caused serious overdose
If treatment is interrupted for more than several days, restart at the lowest dose and re-titrate
moa: Rivastigmine is a reversible carbamate inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, reducing the breakdown of acetylcholine and enhancing cholinergic neurotransmission in the brain, which is deficient in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease dementias.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to rivastigmine, other carbamates, or excipients
Previous severe application-site reaction suggestive of allergic contact dermatitis with the patch (until evaluated)
relative: Bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome or conduction defects
Low body weight (higher risk of GI effects)

preg: Limited human data. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether rivastigmine is excreted in human milk; breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: Clearance may be reduced; titrate to individual tolerability - lower maintenance doses may be required, especially in moderate-to-severe impairment.
hepatic: Exposure is increased in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; titrate to tolerability and use lower maintenance doses.

major: Other cholinomimetics/cholinesterase inhibitors - additive cholinergic toxicity
Anticholinergic drugs - antagonise efficacy and each other
moderate: Beta-blockers and other rate-slowing drugs - additive bradycardia/syncope
Succinylcholine-type muscle relaxants during anaesthesia - exaggerated neuromuscular blockade
NSAIDs - increased gastric acid/ulcer risk with cholinergic stimulation
interactions.food: Take oral forms with food to slow absorption and reduce nausea/vomiting.

serious: Severe vomiting with oesophageal rupture (especially after interruption then restart at high dose)

monitoring: Heart rate and symptoms of bradycardia/syncope
Signs of GI bleeding in at-risk patients
counsel: Take the capsules/liquid with food, morning and evening, to lessen nausea
For patches, apply one a day, rotate the site, and always remove the old patch first
If you stop the medicine for more than a few days, do NOT restart the old dose - contact your doctor to re-titrate
Report a slow heartbeat, fainting, severe vomiting, black stools or a marked skin reaction
Weight loss can occur - mention significant loss of appetite or weight
pk: Cholinergic effects within hours; clinical benefit over weeks
Oral ~1 h; patch steady plasma over the 24-hour wear
Oral ~1.5 h (but cholinesterase inhibition ~10 h); patch effectively longer
Store at 20-25 C; keep patches in sealed pouch until use
pearls: Inhibits both acetyl- and butyryl-cholinesterase (unlike donepezil/galantamine)
Take oral doses with food and titrate slowly to limit GI effects
After any interruption of >several days, re-titrate from the lowest dose - restarting high has caused fatal oesophageal rupture from vomiting
Always remove the old patch before applying a new one - multiple patches cause overdose
Caution with bradycardia, peptic ulcer, asthma/COPD and seizure history
missed: If you miss an oral dose, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time with food - do not double up. If you miss applying a patch, apply a new one as soon as you remember, then continue daily. After missing several days, contact your doctor to re-titrate from the lowest dose.
overdose: Overdose produces a cholinergic crisis - severe nausea, vomiting, salivation, sweating, bradycardia, hypotension, collapse and convulsions. Most asymptomatic overdoses can continue therapy after a 24-hour withhold. For symptomatic overdose give supportive care and atropine (initial ~0.03 mg/kg IV) as the antidote; avoid further rivastigmine until re-titration.
